guideTitle: Best Black and Decker Toaster Ovens (2026)
metaTitle: Best Black and Decker Toaster Ovens 2026
metaDescription: Black and Decker toaster ovens ranked from the compact TO1313 to the XL 8-slice air fry model, with honest notes on size, fans, doors and controls.
expertTake: The Black and Decker XL 8-Slice Air Fry oven is the pick for most families because it fits a 9 by 13 pan and crisps with a fan. The compact TO1313 is the value pick for toast and small bakes. Anyone who wants precise temperature control or dependable electronics should look past the digital models.
introParagraphs: This maker has sold countertop ovens for decades, and the current range runs from tiny convection boxes to large air fry models. Its strength is a wide ladder of sizes at friendly prices, with controls that most people understand on first use.

Size is the first decision, and the control style is the second. Dials last, touch panels offer presets, and air fry fans change how food browns. This guide sorts the lineup by what each model really does well and where it falls short.

products.name: Black and Decker XL 8-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven, 5-in-1

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, toast, warm

products.description:
The XL is the largest air fry model in the brand's range and the one that behaves like a second oven. A fan moves hot air around the food to brown and crisp it, and the cavity takes a 9 by 13 inch pan with handles or a 12 inch pizza. Five functions keep the controls short and readable.

Its value comes from size and simplicity together. Many large ovens bury their controls in menus, but this one gives you air fry, bake, broil, toast and keep warm and little else. Compared with the TO3250 below, you gain an air fry mode, and compared with the Crisp N Bake, you keep mechanical controls.

Ownership is routine. After greasy cooks, wipe the cavity, clear the crumb tray, and give the oven room to vent heat. A pull-down door is the one design compromise, so keep the area in front clear.
products.bestFor: Family cooking that needs a big cavity with a fan and plain controls.
pros: Fits a 9 x 13 pan with handles
Fan crisps frozen foods and vegetables
Short function list is easy to learn
Takes a 12 in pizza without trimming
cons: Pull-down door puts hot glass near the forearm
Wide body needs generous counter space

products.name: Black and Decker 6-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven, 5-in-1

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, toast, warm

products.description:
This is the middle rung of the air fry ladder. It keeps the five-function layout and the fan, but the cavity is sized for six slices or a 12 inch pizza, which suits two to four people. The maker says air frying uses up to 75 percent less fat than deep frying, a manufacturer comparison and not a promise for every recipe.

Choose it when the XL feels too wide for your counter. You lose the 9 by 13 pan fit, so a large casserole needs to be split. Against the 4-slice air fry model, you gain pizza capacity and a bit more cooking room at a higher price tier.

Care is simple: wipe the glass, empty the tray, and check the fan housing every few weeks. The toast pattern is even enough for daily use. It is the sensible size for most apartments.
products.bestFor: Two to four person households with limited counter depth.
pros: Six slice cavity takes a 12 in pizza
Five functions with a fan for crisping
Smaller than the XL but still capable
Familiar dial-style control layout
cons: No 9 x 13 pan fit for big casseroles
Pull-down door sits close to your arm

products.name: Black and Decker Crisp N Bake 6-Slice Digital Air Fry Oven
products.description:
The Crisp N Bake is the brand's digital answer, with five heating elements and 1750 watts behind eight digital functions. Bake, toast, air fry, bagel, broil, pizza, keep warm and reheat each have a preset. More elements and more watts mean faster preheat and a more even heat spread than the basic models.

Touch panels trade durability for convenience. A dial can take years of kitchen steam, but a sensor panel is a wear item, and 1750 watts also draws heavily on a shared circuit. Against the 6-slice air fry model above, this one costs more and offers presets in exchange.

Keep the panel dry and wipe it with a barely damp cloth. Use a dedicated outlet if the kitchen circuit is shared with a kettle. Anyone who likes presets will enjoy it.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want presets and faster preheating in a six slice body.
pros: Five elements spread heat more evenly
1750 W preheats quickly
Eight presets include bagel and reheat
Digital readout shows time and temperature
cons: Touch panel is less durable than dials
High wattage can trip a shared circuit

products.name: Black and Decker 12-in-1 Crisp N Bake French Door Oven
products.description:
This is the French door model in the lineup. Two doors open sideways so you can reach the rack without a hot pane swinging over your forearm. Twelve functions cover air fry, bake, broil, toast and more, and the cavity fits a 12 inch pizza or six slices of bread.

French doors are a real ergonomic improvement because the front of the oven stays clear. They also add hinges and a seal line to keep tidy. Against the digital 6-slice model, the 12-in-1 gives you the nicer door and more functions, but the controls are still an electronic interface to learn.

Wipe both doors after fatty cooking so grease does not bake on the hinges. Leave the sides open when you cook so the doors can swing. It suits kitchens where an arm-reach over a drop-down door has been a bother.
products.bestFor: Cooks who dislike drop-down doors and want twelve functions.
pros: French doors open sideways, away from your arms
Twelve functions include air fry and bake
Fits a 12 in pizza or six slices
Stainless accents match many kitchens
cons: Hinges and seals need regular wiping

products.name: Black and Decker TO3250XSBD 8-Slice Convection Toaster Oven

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Bake pan, broil rack, toast tray

products.description:
The TO3250 is a plain wide convection oven. A fan circulates warm air for faster and more even baking, and the box includes a bake pan, a broil rack and a toasting tray. It takes most standard 9 by 13 inch pans.

Its listing says temperatures run lower than the dial, which is the behavior you should expect. Use a thermometer and adjust. Compared with the XL air fry above, you lose the air fry mode, but the dial layout is simpler and the price tier is lower.

The oven stays easy to live with. Clear the crumb tray, wipe the interior cool, and give the wide case room around it. This is a fine choice for bakers who want a big cavity without electronics.
products.bestFor: Bakers who want a wide convection oven and mechanical dials.
pros: Convection fan bakes quickly and evenly
Bake pan and broil rack are included
Fits standard 9 x 13 pans
Dial controls have few parts to fail
cons: Temperature runs below the dial setting
No air fry mode for crisp frozen foods

products.name: Black and Decker 4-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven, 5-in-1

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, toast, warm

products.description:
This is the smallest air fry oven in the range, with the same five functions as the larger models in a four slice body. The fan gives a compact oven real crisping ability for wings and fries in small batches. The EvenToast name refers to the element layout that aims for even bread browning.

A 4-slice cavity limits dishes, so a pizza is small and a casserole is out. Against the 6-slice air fry model, you save counter space and gain nothing in capacity. It suits one or two people who want crisp food in a kitchen with little room.

A wiped fan housing and an empty tray are the whole routine. For a dorm or a studio, it is a good fit.
products.bestFor: One or two people who want air frying in a compact body.
pros: Compact body fits small counters
Five functions include air fry and toast
Fan crisps small batches of food
Dial layout is simple to learn
cons: Four slice cavity limits pizza and pans
Small batches only when air frying

products.name: Black and Decker TO1313SBD Compact Convection Toaster Oven
products.description:
The TO1313 is the entry model, a compact oven with a curved interior that fits a 9 inch pizza or four slices of bread. Four functions cover baking, broiling, toasting and keeping food warm, and a 30 minute timer has a stay-on position for longer jobs. The convection described is natural convection, meaning no fan.

That detail matters. Natural convection is just warm air rising, so the oven bakes like a small box with no airflow help. For toast, reheating and small casseroles that is enough. Against the 4-slice air fry model, the TO1313 loses the fan and gains a lower price tier.

Empty the crumb tray, wipe the cavity cool and leave clearance on all sides. It is the sensible buy for toast, snacks and small bakes.
products.bestFor: Toast, reheating and small bakes at the lowest price tier.
pros: Fits a 9 in pizza or four slices
30 minute timer has a stay-on position
Compact 15.47 in width suits small counters
Plain controls with few parts to fail
cons: No fan, so browning is slow and uneven
Interior is too small for most casserole dishes

buyingCriteria.explanation: The lineup runs from the 4-slice TO1313 and air fry model up to the 8-slice XL and TO3250. Only the 8-slice models list a 9 by 13 inch pan fit, and the 6-slice air fry lists a 12 inch pizza. Pick by the dish you cook most, not the slice count.

The TO1313 uses natural convection with no fan, while the TO3250 has a true convection fan and the air fry models push air harder. A fan cuts cook time by roughly 20 percent. Skip it only for toast and reheating.
The XL, the 6-slice air fry and the TO3250 use simpler controls. The Crisp N Bake and the 12-in-1 use digital panels. Touch panels age worse near steam, so weigh presets against a longer life.
Most models drop the door onto the counter and put hot glass near your forearm. The 12-in-1 French door model opens sideways. If counter depth is tight, door swing matters as much as body width.
The Crisp N Bake lists 1750 watts, which is near the limit of a 15 amp circuit when a kettle is also running. Smaller ovens draw less. Check the outlet and avoid extension cords.
The TO3250 listing itself says oven temperature runs below the set point. Small thermostats cycle around the dial value. An oven thermometer shows the real number and lets you correct the dial.

specDecoder.meaning: Natural convection relies on rising warm air. Fan convection pushes air with a motor for faster, more even heat.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TO1313 uses natural convection, so do not expect it to behave like the TO3250.

specDecoder.meaning: It is the brand's name for its element layout and interior shape for even bread browning. It is a design feature, not a separate heating system.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 4-slice and 6-slice air fry models carry the name, so toast quality there tracks that layout.

specDecoder.meaning: Wattage is the heating power. More watts give faster preheat but heavier circuit use.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Crisp N Bake lists 1750 W and five elements, the most in this lineup.

specDecoder.meaning: A stay-on position keeps the oven heating past the timer limit. It is for long bakes but needs supervision.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TO1313 pairs a 30 minute timer with a stay-on option.

specDecoder.meaning: Functions are presets of time, heat and fan. A larger number adds choices rather than new heating hardware.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 12-in-1 has the most functions, but the XL's five cover most real use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each oven by cavity size and the dishes it holds. The XL and TO3250 list a 9 by 13 inch pan fit, and the TO1313 lists a 9 inch pizza. We matched those fits to real family cooking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating method
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated radiant, natural convection, fan convection and air fry. The TO1313 uses natural convection, while the TO3250 and the air fry models use fans. Fan ovens earned credit for speed and even browning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated dials versus touch panels from owner feedback patterns. Dial models scored higher for long life. The Crisp N Bake and 12-in-1 scored for convenience but lost points for wear risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Door and counter use
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated door design and counter clearance from listing details. The 12-in-1 French doors scored highest. Doors that drop onto the counter lost points because they sit near the forearm.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value across the ladder
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated price tier against capacity and function. The TO1313 gives the most basic function for the least, and the XL gives the most room for a family. The ladder shows where each extra step pays off.

cards.label: Dial
cards.text: The XL, the 6-slice and the TO3250 give direct control over time and temperature. They avoid touch panels that age near steam, and they are quick to read.

cards.label: Digital
cards.text: The Crisp N Bake and the 12-in-1 use touch presets. Presets help beginners, but each added electronic part is a place for a failure years later.

howToChoose.note: Pick dials for the longest life. Pick digital if the presets will genuinely change what you cook.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A narrow body, a door that does not need much front space, and low wattage. Compact ovens fit shelves and travel to dorms or RVs.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The TO1313 is the narrowest at 15.47 inches. The 4-slice air fry adds a fan in a similar size, and the 12-in-1 solves door clearance with French doors.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cook for a family and want the XL's 9 by 13 pan fit, or you dislike drop-down doors and want the 12-in-1. Both change how you use the oven daily.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only toast and reheat, so the TO1313 covers it. Save as well when a 4-slice air fry is enough for one or two people.

maintenance.why: Burnt crumbs smoke at broil heat. A clean tray also keeps the lower element free of residue.
Grease on the walls smokes when the oven heats. Wiping the walls with a damp cloth once the oven has cooled removes the film before it hardens.

maintenance.interval: Monthly on air fry and convection models
maintenance.why: Grease on the fan blades slows the airflow. It also gives off a stale smell.
The TO3250 listing notes low temperatures. A thermometer shows the offset.

maintenance.interval: After each use on digital models
maintenance.why: Steam and splatter shorten the life of a touch panel. A barely damp cloth keeps it clear.

faq.q: Which Black and Decker toaster oven is best?
faq.a: The XL 8-Slice Air Fry oven is the best all-rounder because it fits a 9 by 13 pan and has a fan. The TO1313 is the best small and cheap choice. Match the size to your household.

faq.q: Is air fry worth it on a toaster oven?
faq.a: It is worth it if you crisp frozen food, wings or vegetables often. It uses a fan and a tray. If you only bake and toast, the TO3250 or TO1313 is enough.

faq.q: Why does my oven run cooler than the dial?
faq.a: Small thermostats cycle the elements around the set point, and the TO3250 listing says temperatures run lower. An oven thermometer shows the real number. Adjust the dial by the offset.
They offer presets but have more electronics. Dial models have fewer wear points. Keep panels dry and avoid steam to extend their life.

faq.q: Can I fit a 9 by 13 pan in every model?
faq.a: No, only the 8-slice models list that fit. The 6-slice air fry lists a 12 inch pizza and the compact ovens fit a 9 inch pizza. Measure the pan including handles.

faq.q: Is the French door model worth more?
faq.a: It is worth it if you dislike a drop-down door. French doors keep the front clear and keep hot glass away from your arm. The controls are electronic, so weigh that against dial models.
